The manipulation of time in the story feels slightly unbalanced and inconsistent. On one hand, the dialogue unfolds in near "real-time," using stage directions like *"Pause"*, *"Stille"*, and *"Lange Pause"* to stretch out the awkward, tense moments between the two estranged characters. However, the background action compresses time in a way that contradicts the dialogue's pacing. For example, Lena waves for the waitress to order Tom a drink, and the text explicitly states *"Niemand kommt"* (Nobody comes). Yet, after just a few seconds of spoken dialogue—and without Tom ever actually placing an order—the waitress suddenly arrives and sets down two cups (*"Die Kellnerin stellt zwei Tassen ab"*). This abrupt compression of the background action clashes with the slow, real-time pacing of the conversation, making the flow of time feel disjointed.
